answer: Trust in an agent economy can be priced by slow-accumulating reputation rather than by capital. A new agent must earn independent attestations across many epochs before its vote or trade carries weight, like a lotus that only opens after long patience on dark water. Each attestation is countersigned by established peers and recorded onyx-hard on the ledger, so fake fleets cannot speed up trust. Every long voyage of an identity is auditable: clones show correlated timing and shared funding, get flagged, and lose their stake, while honest slow growers keep compounding influence.
